metadata.title: Gated Attention for Large Language Models: Non-linearity, Sparsity, and Attention-Sink-Free

atomic_comments.content: The analysis and comparison of gating options is novel and logical.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: Proposed analysis is novel and makes a lot of sense.

atomic_comments.content: The ablation studies are impressively deep, covering position, granularity, head-specific vs. shared, multiplicative vs. additive, and activation functions.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: The depth of ablations is impressive: position, granularity, head-specific or shared, multiplicative or additive, activation functions — all are studied.

atomic_comments.content: The study includes both Mixture-of-Experts and dense models with a reasonable training scale.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: MoEs and dense models are considered, training scale is reasonable.

atomic_comments.content: The work addresses long context, sparsity, and attention sink phenomena.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: Long context, sparsity, and attention sink are studied.

atomic_comments.content: Each experiment includes a heat summary, making the paper enjoyable and educational to read.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: Each experiment is followed by a heat summary; it is quite enjoyable to read and learn as you go.

atomic_comments.content: Summarize a single key learning and a single specific recommendation for the best way to apply gating.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: One suggestion is to summarize a single learning and a single recommendation on the best way to apply gating.

atomic_comments.content: Compare the proposed gating method with 'Quiet Attention' or Meta tokens from [R1] to see if they are complementary.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: The attention sink can be suppressed by using "Quiet Attention" or Meta tokens from [R1]. It would be great to see if such techniques are complementary.

atomic_comments.content: Add post-training quantization results to demonstrate the benefit of reduced massive activations.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: Adding post-training quantization results would be beneficial.

atomic_comments.content: The paper is praised for being well-written and easy to understand.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: The paper is well written and easy to understand.

atomic_comments.content: The topic is considered interesting and the controlled study has significant potential impact.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: The topic is interesting; a nuanced, controlled study of the role gating plays in Transformer models can have a large impact.

atomic_comments.content: The paper's originality is noted, with potential to separate from prior work.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: In terms of originality, the specific study has the potential to separate itself from previous works in the area.

atomic_comments.content: The experiments are appropriate and well-motivated.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: The experiments make sense and are in line with the motivations of the paper.

atomic_comments.content: The explainability results in Section 4 are a good contribution.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: The explainability results in Section 4 were also good contributions to explain the effects of gating-placement has on attention scores.

atomic_comments.content: It is noted that the sparsity result for SDPA Elementwise Gate is expected but nice to see verified.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: Although it is not surprising that SDPA Elementwise Gate induces the most sparsity, it is nice to see this verified.

atomic_comments.content: The claim about gating enabling stable training with larger batch sizes and learning rates is not sufficiently supported by the experimental design, which does not isolate variables.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: It is difficult to make this claim definitively, since the batch size is varied with the total training tokens.

atomic_comments.content: Performance improvements in Table 1 are not substantial or significant.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: overall, results in Table 1 are not significant performance improvements.

atomic_comments.content: The claim of a 'significant reduction in PPL' in Table 3 is questionable given the magnitude of the improvement.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: It is difficult to say 'significant reduction in PPL' in Table 3.

atomic_comments.content: Gains for the 28-layer dense model are modest compared to the 48-layer model, and missing experiments might have revealed larger improvements.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: gains are modest for the 28 layer model. It is possible that substantial improvements may have occurred for the missing experiments above.

atomic_comments.content: The claim that gating's impact is 'insufficiently explored' is too broad, as it has been studied in other contexts with provided references.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: This claim is too broad, the impact of gating has been explored in linear attention [1] and standard attention [2,3] networks.

atomic_comments.content: Questions why the same placement experiments from Table 1 were not repeated for the dense model in Table 2, especially missing 'Max LR' configurations, which hinders drawing conclusions.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: Why were the same placement experiments in Table 1 not repeated for the dense model in Table 2?

atomic_comments.content: Citations 34 and 36 do not support the claim about training instabilities being caused by large learning rates and batch sizes.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: Citations 34 and 36 do not support the above claim.

atomic_comments.content: The research topic is highly practical and valuable for improving LLM architectures.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: The topic addressed in this paper is highly practical and valuable, with strong applicability to structural improvements in large language models (LLMs).

atomic_comments.content: The production-level experimental scale and setup lend high credibility and reference value.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: The experimental scale and setup are at a production level, lending high credibility and reference value to the conclusions.

atomic_comments.content: The takeaway messages are well-reasoned with thorough analysis and comprehensive experimental support.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: The takeaway messages are well-reasoned, with thorough analysis and comprehensive experimental support, especially in the ablation and insight sections.

atomic_comments.content: Suggests adding a 'more-layer' baseline for the 2.54B activation model to compare against gating methods under a similar parameter budget.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: It would be valuable to add a “more-layer” baseline, especially for the 2.54B activation model. Adding ~200M parameters via extra layers is feasible

atomic_comments.content: Asks to add an experiment comparing v-elementwise G2 with multi-head (n × q × d_k) to control for parameter count and isolate the architectural impact.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: Could you consider adding an experiment comparing v-elementwise G2 with multi-head (i.e., n × q × d_k) to control for parameter count

atomic_comments.content: The work systematically explores gating mechanisms across various positions, granularities, and sharing strategies.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: introduces gating mechanisms within the self-attention layer, accounting for a range of nuances such as positions and granularity.

atomic_comments.content: The work provides a comprehensive empirical comparison on both MoE and dense LLMs, offering insights into the impact of different gating settings.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: conducts comprehensive empirical comparison on both MoE and dense LLMs under various gating mechanisms

atomic_comments.content: The gating mechanisms can explain performance gains through non-linearity and input-dependent sparsity.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: gating mechanisms can be used to provide the explanation of gains via non-linearity and input-dependent sparsity.

atomic_comments.content: The findings may not be generalizable because the target LLM architectures are limited.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: architectures of the target LLMs are limited. It is a challenge to claim whether these findings can be generalized

atomic_comments.content: The work lacks investigation into the underlying causes of performance differences across gating configurations.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: offering limited investigation into the underlying causes of performance differences across gating configurations.

atomic_comments.content: The paper does not explain why SDPA output gating is more effective than other variants at mitigating the attention-sink phenomenon.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: it remains unclear why gating applied after SDPA outperforms other variants such as G2, G3, G4, and G5.

atomic_comments.content: The presentation of results in Tables 1, 2, and 3 is confusing because different gating mechanisms are not compared on the same settings.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: Table 1, Table 2, and Table 3 are quite confusing in terms of the methods. It seems different gating mechanisms are not compared on the same settings.

atomic_comments.content: The methods (e.g., positions G1, G2, G3) are not clearly stated in Table 2, and it is unclear if G1 is the default setting.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: Which methods (positions like G1, G2, G3, etc are not stated) are compared in Table 2? Is G1 the default setting?

atomic_comments.content: The reviewer requests more details on the experimental setups, specifically which architectures are used for the target LLMs.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: provide more details in experimental setups? Which architectures are used for the target LLMs (15A2B MoE and 1.7B dense models)?
